brief: Goldman Sachs Prime Services data on US hedge fund positioning and flows for August 28 to September 3, as of 5 September 2026. The note reports and does not argue: each aggregate move is attributed to its components, with no forecast or recommendation. Gross leverage rose 1.5 points to 208.5%, the 27th percentile of the past year, net leverage rose 0.9 points to 48.4%, the 4th percentile, and the fundamental long/short ratio rose 0.5% to 1.605, also 4th percentile. US equities were slightly net bought at +0.2 standard deviations because long buying in single stocks outweighed short selling in single stocks and macro products. Macro products, index and ETF combined, were net sold at -0.3 standard deviations, almost entirely short sales, with US-listed ETF shorts up 1.5% on the week and down 4.4% month over month, led by credit and small cap shorting against large cap covering. Single stocks were net bought for the first time in three weeks, long buys to short sales 1.6 to 1, into info tech, communication services, financials and utilities, out of real estate, energy, industrials and staples. Real estate was net sold a fourth straight week at the fastest pace in nearly seven months.
